subparts.method: Original O,A,B,C are on orthogonal axes with OA4,OB12/5,OC3. CA=(4,0,−3) has length5, and pointP is ON CA with CP3, so CP=(3/5)CA=(12/5,0,−9/5). This establishes the requested printed vector, not a coordinate estimate from the picture.
Use OP=OC+CP, including the ORIGINAL height3 offset. CP alone is not the position ofP fromO.
Use BP=OP−OB with ORIGINAL B=(0,12/5,0). Keep the negative j component and the arrow direction BtoP.

The target angle is BPC. Chosen BP andCP both point INTO the common vertexP, so their dot product gives the same angle as the two OUTGOING raysPB andPC. Their dot is18/5 and norms18/5,3, giving cos(theta)=1/3. Reversing just one arrow without supplementing the angle would instead give109.5 degrees.
